runaway_hand.speaker: narrator
runaway_hand.text: Patch put the shears down on the paper, a long way out of reach, and knelt in the ink in front of him.

runaway_hand.speaker: runaway
runaway_hand.text: Go on. You've cut everything else in the book. Do the one that matters.

runaway_hand.speaker: runaway
runaway_hand.text: I pulled my tail out of her hands. I heard her go under, and I ran, and I kept running till the water stopped. You don't get to forgive that. Nobody does.

runaway_hand.speaker: patch
runaway_hand.text: I know. I'm not here to forgive it. I'm here because you're me, and I'm tired of leaving you out here on your own.

runaway_hand.speaker: patch
runaway_hand.text: It still happened. I'm going to carry it. Both of us are. Give me your paw.

runaway_hand.speaker: narrator
runaway_hand.text: The Runaway looked at the paw held out to him for a long time. Then he took it, and the ink began to run off him like rain off a window, and the fox underneath was the same fox, all the way through.

true_ending.speaker: narrator
true_ending.text: Weeks later. A rented flat, two rooms and a kitchen, with boxes still stacked in the corner that nobody had the heart to open. Rain on the window. One lamp.

true_ending.speaker: nell
true_ending.text: I couldn't sleep. I was looking at the back page. The blank one.

true_ending.speaker: nell
true_ending.text: Before I drew on it I wrote something. In pen. I wrote it was ruined, and I crossed it out, and I wrote it again. I was so angry at it, Dad. At the book. At you, for not stopping.

true_ending.speaker: dad
true_ending.text: I know. I could hear you thinking it.

true_ending.speaker: nell
true_ending.text: Look, though. Right at the bottom, in the margin, under all of that. The fox is there. Two of him. Holding paws.

true_ending.speaker: gran
true_ending.text: Books do that, if you leave them room. Something comes back for the bit of itself it left behind.

true_ending.speaker: nell
true_ending.text: Gran. You're supposed to be asleep.

true_ending.speaker: gran
true_ending.text: I'm waiting for the kettle. What's the empty one for?

true_ending.speaker: dad
true_ending.text: I bought it today. I thought we'd start another. A second one. It won't be the same.

true_ending.speaker: nell
true_ending.text: It doesn't have to be the same.

true_ending.speaker: nell
true_ending.text: Can the fox be in it?

true_ending.speaker: dad
true_ending.text: He's in all of them now.

true_ending.speaker: narrator
true_ending.text: Nell opened the new book to its first page, and wrote at the top of it, slowly, so she wouldn't have to cross it out.

true_ending.speaker: nell_hand
true_ending.text: SECOND PRINTING. For everyone who ran, and came back.
